newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon bans import of agricultural products.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon bans import of agricultural products.

text.p: Lebanon will halt as of October 1 the import of agricultural products that can be homegrown in an attempt to boost productivity and activate the agro-industry, the minister of agriculture said on Thursday.
Minister Shawki Fakhoury was commenting on a decision taken at a late night cabinet session to dramatically slash the $1 billion food and vegetable import bill.
"This is a historic decision. It is the first time Lebanon takes a decision aiming at protecting the Lebanese farmer and agriculture," Fakhoury told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri said after Wednesday's session that the cabinet instructed Fakhoury to present within one month a list of agricultural items to be exempted from the import ban as they are needed by Lebanese industry.
"The import of classical products like tomatoes, potatoes, lettuce or cucumbers, will be halted," Hariri said in remarks published by Beirut newspapers.
Fakhoury said Lebanon was self-sufficient in milk and green vegetables.
"There will be no exemption with regard to milk and green vegetables but we will still have to import some fruits and meat products," he added.
Hariri said the decision could alter Lebanon's image from a major food importer to an exporter.
"Not too long ago we banned the import of bananas, and after a very short period of time, Lebanon turned from an importer of bananas to an exporter of the product," he said.
"Lebanon imports large quantities of flowers from Holland, at a time when we can produce flowers in Lebanon," he added.

In 1996, Lebanon imported food and vegetable products worth $1.058 billion -- 14 percent of its total imports of $7.559 billion while it exported $132 million worth of these products -- 13 percent of the total $1.018 exports bill.
Hariri said the decision was the first step in a plan aimed at stimulating growth and activating the economy. He said the cabinet decided to prepare a draft law to promote investments in Lebanon.

"We have agreed to prepare a draft law to promote investment in all sectors in Lebanese regions. It should be ready within a few weeks to be discussed by the cabinet in order to be sent to parliament (for approval)," Hariri said.
Fakhoury said Syria, Egypt, Jordan and Saudi Arabia topped the list of countries exporting food and farm products to Lebanon.
A recent ban on the import of Egyptian potatoes angered Cairo which protested against the decision at the Lebanese foreign ministry.
"I will make a tour of some Arab countries to clarify the decision," Fakhouri added.
